summary: The correlated Office-to-PowerShell chain, startup artifact and malware detection support malicious activity.

findings.statement: An Office process spawned PowerShell, which connected externally and wrote a user startup script.
The startup write combined with the malware detection on the same file supports a malicious persistence chain.

alternative_explanations.explanation: An approved Office automation workflow could launch PowerShell.
alternative_explanations.assessment: That does not adequately explain the startup script and matching malware detection; investigate authorization without ignoring affirmative evidence.

recommendations.description: Ask an authorized operator to review containment; preserve the startup file and investigate scope. No action has been executed.
recommendations.rationale: The correlated Office-to-PowerShell chain, startup artifact and malware detection support malicious activity.

limitations: Synthetic contract fixture, not observed endpoint telemetry.
Only the supplied time window and log sources are represented.
